title: Machine learning and cell assays prioritize FASN in a smoking–male-infertility study
summary: Researchers at Meishan City Second People’s Hospital integrated three infertility transcriptomic datasets with network toxicology and used LASSO and support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination to prioritize candidate genes. The publisher abstract reports a genetic association between higher predicted FASN expression and male-infertility risk and increased FASN mRNA after cigarette-smoke-condensate exposure in mouse TM4 Sertoli cells. These findings nominate FASN for functional investigation; they do not show that FASN mediates smoke-induced reproductive injury or establish a treatment. This source check covers the publisher abstract, affiliations and publication metadata; full methods were not assessed.
ai_technology: LASSO; support vector machine recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE)

evidence.tested: Transcriptomic candidate selection and MR/SMR genetic associations, plus a within-study RT-qPCR assay reporting increased FASN mRNA in mouse TM4 Sertoli cells after smoke-condensate exposure.
evidence.unknown: The source explicitly states that FASN-mediated smoke-induced injury is not established. Full-paper methods and supplements were not assessed; human causal mediation and therapeutic benefit are unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO and SVM-RFE select candidate genes from integrated target and transcriptomic features, helping prioritize FASN for genetic analyses and a bounded cell-expression test.

source_review.scope: Publisher abstract, affiliations, publication metadata and visible ethics/data statements; subscription full paper not assessed
